'''Oleg Borisovich Lupanov''' ({{langx|ru|Оле́г Бори́сович Лупа́нов}}; 2 June 1932 – 3 May 2006) was a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Russia]]n [[mathematician]], dean of the [[Moscow State University]]'s [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] (1980–2006), head of the Chair of [[Discrete Mathematics]] of the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] (1981–2006).<ref name="russianwikiarticle">[[:ru:Лупанов|Oleg Borisovich Lupanov, a Russian Wikipedia entry]]</ref>

Together with his graduate school advisor, [[Sergey Yablonsky]], he is considered one of the founders of the Soviet school of [[Cybernetics|Mathematical Cybernetics]]. In particular he authored pioneering works on synthesis and complexity of [[Boolean circuits]], and of [[control systems]] in general ({{langx|ru|Управляющие системы}}), the term used in the [[Soviet Union|USSR]] and [[Russia]] for a generalization of [[finite-state automata]], [[Boolean circuits]] and [[multi-valued logic]] [[logic circuit|circuit]]s.

[[Ingo Wegener]], in his book ''The Complexity of Boolean Functions,''<ref name="WegenerBook">[[Ingo Wegener|I. Wegener]], The Complexity of Boolean Functions [http://eccc.hpi-web.de/eccc-local/ECCC-Books/wegener_book_readme.html]. John Wiley and Sons Ltd, and B. G. Teubner, Stuttgart, 1987. page 87.</ref> credits O. B. Lupanov for coining the term ''[[Claude Shannon|Shannon]] effect'' in his 1970 paper,<ref name="Lupanov70">O. B. Lupanov, On circuits of functional elements with delay. Problemy Kibernetiki, Vol. 23, 1970, pp. 43–81.</ref> to refer to the fact that almost all Boolean functions have nearly the same circuit complexity as the hardest function.

O. B. Lupanov is best known for his (''k'',&nbsp;''s'')-Lupanov representation of Boolean functions<ref name="Lupanov58">O. B. Lupanov, A method of circuit synthesis. Izvesitya VUZ, Radiofizika Vol. 1, 1958, pp. 120–140.</ref> that he used to devise an asymptotically optimal method of Boolean circuit synthesis, thus proving the asymptotically tight upper bound on Boolean circuit complexity:

: <math>C(f)\le \frac{2^n}{n} + o\left(\frac{2^n}{n}\right). </math>

== Biography ==
O. B. Lupanov graduated from [[Moscow State University]]'s [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] in 1955. He received his [[Kandidat|PhD]] in 1958 from the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]] and his Doctorate degree in 1963. He began teaching at [[Moscow State University]] in 1959 and became professor there in 1967. From 1955 he had appointment at the [[Keldysh Institute of Applied Mathematics|Institute of Applied Mathematics]] and he was a professor at [[MSU Faculty of Computational Mathematics and Cybernetics|Faculty of Computational Mathematics and Cybernetics]] (1970–1980). He had served as the Dean of the [[Moscow State University]]'s [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] (1980–2006), and as the founding head of the Chair of [[Discrete Mathematics]] of the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] (1981–2006).<ref name="russianwikiarticle"/>

Lupanov became a corresponding member of the Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union in 1972 and a full member of Russian Academy of Sciences in 2003. He was the lead scientist of the [[Keldysh Institute of Applied Mathematics]] since 1993 and was awarded the title of a distinguished professor of Moscow State University in 2002. He was a recipient of the prestigious [[Lenin Prize]] (1966) and of the [[Moscow State University]]'s [[Lomonosov Award]] (1993).

His students count more than 30 [[Kandidat|PhD]] degree holders and 6 holders of the [[Doctorate#Doctorates in Russia|Soviet/Russian Doctorate degree]].<ref name="msu bio">[http://www.math.msu.su/biography/lupruss.htm Biography of O. B. Lupanov at Moscow State University's website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807233814/http://www.math.msu.su/biography/lupruss.htm |date=2011-08-07 }}</ref> As a dean of the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]], he was known as a democratic and accessible person.<ref name="site1001">Владимир Шахиджанян (Vladimir Shakhidzhanyan), An entrepreneur's diary, 1001 website, Published July 31, 2006 [http://1001.vdv.ru/arc/businessman/issue918/]</ref>

== Personal life ==
Lupanov died at around 7pm on 3 May 2006 in his office at the [[MSU Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics|Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics]] of [[Moscow State University]].
